subject.title: feat: expose rawBody on user messages in plugin hook events

question: Should plugin hooks expose literal `RawBody`, command-normalized direct-user text, or wait for the shared trusted inbound-body contract?
rationale: Existing OpenClaw contracts distinguish raw body from command-processing text, while this branch combines them under one permanent external field name.

options.title: Expose clean direct-user text
options.body: Use a non-literal name aligned with current body vocabulary, retain provenance gating, and document the cross-runtime minimum plus embedded steer refinement.

options.title: Expose literal RawBody
options.body: Source only the literal unwrapped channel body and keep command-normalized input separate.

options.title: Wait for shared inbound metadata
options.body: Pause until the trusted inbound-decoration work defines the canonical clean-input source.

recommendation.title: Expose clean direct-user text
recommendation.body: Use a non-literal name aligned with current body vocabulary, retain provenance gating, and document the cross-runtime minimum plus embedded steer refinement.

likelyOwner.reason: The central current-main plugin hook type history makes this the best available API decision route.
